info.title: Smart Glasses Middleware API
info.description:
A comprehensive middleware API for smart glasses that processes audio, images, videos, and text with AI-powered task detection and intelligent routing. Features include RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) indexing for all uploaded files, making them easily searchable and referenceable by AI.

## Global Headers

All API responses include the following headers for tracing and debugging:

- **X-Request-Id**: A unique identifier for each request. This can be used to correlate requests with server logs.
- **X-Correlation-ID**: A correlation identifier that can be provided by the client or will be auto-generated. This allows tracking requests across multiple services.

### Correlation ID Usage

Clients can provide a correlation ID in the request:
```
X-Correlation-ID: <your-correlation-id>
```

If not provided, the server will generate one and include it in the response. The same correlation ID should be used when making related requests to trace a complete workflow.

## Rate Limiting

The API implements rate limiting to ensure fair usage. By default, clients are limited to 60 requests per minute.

When rate limited, the API returns a 429 status code with a ProblemDetails response.

## Error Handling

The API uses RFC 7807 Problem Details for consistent error responses. All errors return a JSON object with the following structure:

```json
{
  "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.1",
  "title": "Error Title",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "Detailed error message",
  "instance": "/api/endpoint",
  "requestId": "unique-request-id",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

get.description:
Checks the health status of all dependent services including PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO, Ollama AI, and the Vosk transcription service. 
Returns a comprehensive health report with individual service statuses.

This endpoint is used for monitoring and should not be cached. It's designed for use by load balancers, orchestration systems, and monitoring tools.

post.summary: Process media files (images, videos, audio) with optional AI prompt
post.description:
Accepts multipart/form-data with media files and optional prompts. All uploaded files are stored in MinIO, processed through RAG indexing, and analyzed by AI. Audio files are automatically transcribed. This endpoint supports multiple file uploads and processes them asynchronously. Fields:
- files: One or more media files (images, videos, audio)
- prompt: Optional text prompt for AI processing
- promptAudio: Optional audio file containing the prompt (mutually exclusive with prompt)
- manifest: Optional JSON array specifying file processing order
- perFileTranscriptions: Optional JSON object mapping filenames to transcriptions

Supported file formats:
- Images: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif
- Videos: .mp4, .avi, .mov
- Audio: .wav, .mp3, .m4a, .flac, .aac

requestBody.description: Media request containing files and optional prompt

value.response: I see a beach scene with people and umbrellas.
Reminder set for tomorrow at 3 PM

get.description: Retrieves the status and result for a background processing task created by /api/ask.

Returns application-level metrics including request counts, error rates, and response times per endpoint.

**Authentication:** In production environments, this endpoint requires an X-API-Key header for authentication.

This endpoint is designed for monitoring and observability tools like Prometheus, Grafana, or custom dashboards.

401.description: Unauthorized - API key missing or invalid

403.description: Forbidden - API key not configured in production

parameters.name: X-API-Key
parameters.description: API key for accessing metrics in production (not required in development)

get.description: Retrieves a paginated list of all files uploaded through the admin panel. All files returned have been processed through the RAG system for AI searchability. Supports caching for improved performance.

post.summary: Upload a new file with label
post.description: Uploads a file to MinIO storage, saves metadata to PostgreSQL, and automatically processes it through the RAG system for AI indexing. The file becomes immediately searchable and referenceable by AI. Files are deduplicated by content hash - if the same file is uploaded again, the existing file is returned instead of creating a duplicate.

201.description: File uploaded successfully and processed for RAG

400.description: Bad Request - Missing file or label

value.title: Internal Server Error
value.detail: An error occurred while uploading the file

post.summary: Invalidate specific cache or all caches
post.description: Invalidates the specified caches or all caches if no targets are provided. Targets can include 'files', 'prompts', and 'groups'.

targets.description: List of cache targets to invalidate. If empty or null, all caches are invalidated.
